transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jess Carter (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Alice Nguyen (Solaris PM), Tom Rivera (Solaris ML Eng), Priya Shah (Solaris Security), Marcus Li (CTO joined at 00:48)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/solaris-poc, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/solaris-pilot, sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Goal: scope a 4-week POC focusing on integration using Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs; validate latency p95 and throughput targets and measure cost per 1M tokens.
- Key success criteria discussed: p95 latency < 250ms for short chat flows, sustained 800 qps for embeddings batch scenario, end-to-end structured outputs for downstream ingestion.
- Security: VPC/private deployment and KMS integration required; customer to validate SOC2 artifacts.
- Next steps: share pricing/SOW, run benchmark with sample logs, provide SDK examples and function-calling templates.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jess Carter: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jess with Redwood, I'm the AE on this, with me is Raj our SE. how's it going alice?
[00:08] Alice Nguyen: hey Jess, thanks, excited to dig in. we've got Tom and Priya from eng and security, respectively.
[00:13] Raj Patel: uh hi all, quick agenda, we'll cover success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, then dive into integration — SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling and structured output. sound good?
[00:22] Tom Rivera: yep sounds good. just want to make sure we get the throughput numbers set, we're trying to avoid surprises.
[00:27] Priya Shah: and i need to confirm encryption, SSO and audit log requirements — SOC2 is a must for our compliance team.
[00:34] Jess Carter: totally, we'll cover that. to kick off, alice can you share current use cases and what you want from the pilot?
[00:41] Alice Nguyen: sure. primary use case is a customer-facing chat assistant that summarizes account activity and recommends next steps — about 60% chat (short prompts), 30% embeddings-based search for knowledge base, 10% batch inference for nightly reranking. target is to move from prototype to production in 3 months if pilot goes well.
[01:00] Raj Patel: good. for sizing, can you give rough numbers — average prompt length, concurrent users, peak qps, and embedding sizes?
[01:07] Alice Nguyen: average chat prompt ~ 120 tokens, responses ~ 200 tokens. concurrent active users 2k, estimated peak QPS ~ 350 for chat flows, embeddings combo is batch up to 50 concurrent embedding requests each with 1-2k vectors for nightly index updates.
[01:25] Tom Rivera: on cache, we expect a lot of repeated prefixes, so hope Redwood's prefix/KV cache will cut cost.
[01:33] Raj Patel: yes, our runtime supports prefix caching and continuous batching. for chat we usually recommend a target p95 latency of <250ms for short flows with small batch sizes to keep tail latency low. for embeddings batch we size for throughput more than latency.
[01:48] Alice Nguyen: what's the expected cost ballpark for that QPS? even rough numbers help us size budget.
[01:53] Jess Carter: i'll put a very rough estimate in the follow-up pricing but to ballpark: with optimistic batching and caching, pilot could run low thousands per month, production depending on commit could be in the mid-5 digits — but we'll provide a tailored estimate after we see logs.
[02:07] Marcus Li: (joined) sorry i'm late, just catching up — curious about model choices. we prefer open models but need performance; can you map variants to latency/cost?
[02:16] Raj Patel: yeah, we maintain a model catalog. for chat we often test a 13B quantized variant for low-latency and cost; if you need higher quality we can swap to a 33B or higher. we can also route fallbacks to hosted variants if Dedicated capacity spikes.
[02:33] Tom Rivera: how do we integrate? we're already using OpenAI-compatible endpoints for dev — would Redwood's API be a drop-in?
[02:40] Raj Patel: we offer OpenAI-compatible endpoints for text generation, chat, embeddings; most SDKs are small wrappers. we also provide first-class SDKs in python/node and a sample repo; plus function calling/tool-calling support that mirrors OpenAI's function calling schema.
[02:54] Alice Nguyen: important for us is structured output — we need JSON responses with fixed keys to feed downstream pipelines. is that supported?
[03:01] Raj Patel: absolutely, we have structured output tooling and output parsers. we can enforce JSON schema in the model response layer and validate during the benchmark — we also provide a post-processing SDK helper that does schema validation and minor repair heuristics.
[03:16] Priya Shah: on security, we require VPC/private control plane, customer-managed KMS integration, SAML SSO, and audit logs retained for 1 year. does Redwood support those?
[03:25] Jess Carter: yes, our Private deployment supports VPC and on-prem options; KMS/HSM integrations are available, SAML SSO and RBAC are in the console, and we can extend log retention per enterprise add-on. we'll attach the SOC2 and our security pack after the call.
[03:40] Tom Rivera: for the pilot, we want to run a focused benchmark. recommended approach?
[03:44] Raj Patel: typical pilot is two phases: integration + smoke tests (1 week) then performance benchmarks (1 week). we'll take your 7-day logs, replay representative traffic — measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. for embeddings, measure throughput for the nightly batch and end-to-end ingestion time.
[04:03] Alice Nguyen: timeline-wise we were hoping for a 4-week pilot — first two weeks integration and small-scale testing, second two weeks run full benchmarks and iterate. is that realistic?
[04:12] Jess Carter: yes that maps to our standard. we usually do an initial week for onboarding and SDK integration, then a week for smoke tests, then schedule the benchmark run. overall 4 weeks is doable.
[04:22] Raj Patel: on the integration side, simplest is to use our OpenAI-compatible endpoints — you can switch the base URL and most dev work is zero to minimal. for advanced function/tool calling we have example manifests and typed schemas.
[04:36] Tom Rivera: how about streaming and partial responses — we rely on streaming for progressive UI updates.
[04:40] Raj Patel: streaming is supported; we stream tokens and also provide structured event hooks for tool invocation and function call events. some older SDK clients may show slight differences but our python/node SDKs handle streaming cleanly.
[04:53] Alice Nguyen: are there known gotchas migrating from OpenAI endpoints?
[04:57] Raj Patel: small differences: model names, certain optional params, and our rate limit semantics. also our dedicated pools might require different endpoint prefixes. we'll share a migration checklist.
[05:07] Marcus Li: what about observability — we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns.
[05:12] Jess Carter: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency and model dashboards, trace ids and request replay hooks. we'll show a short demo in the follow-up if helpful.
[05:24] Priya Shah: audit logs and retention — you said that can be configured, is there an SLA?
[05:29] Jess Carter: audit logs are part of the enterprise package; we can include them in the SOW. retention and export options will be specified in the addendum.
[05:38] Tom Rivera: ok, on benchmarks, what metrics should we set as acceptance criteria for pilot success?
[05:44] Raj Patel: we recommend a set: 1) functional correctness: structured output matches schema for 95% of test prompts; 2) latency: p95 < 250ms for chat short flows and p95 < 800ms for longer context calls; 3) throughput: sustain 80% of your peak QPS for at least 30m in load test; 4) cost: cost per 1M tokens within 20% of target estimate. those are negotiable.
[06:10] Alice Nguyen: interesting. for functional correctness, how do you validate? we have prompt sets and golden outputs.
[06:15] Raj Patel: perfect — we'll run your prompt set through and compute schema compliance, exact match on critical fields, and semantic similarity metrics. we can also add human review for ambiguous cases.
[06:26] Jess Carter: to make this concrete — can you commit to sharing sample logs and the prompt/expected-output set in the next week?
[06:33] Alice Nguyen: yes, tom will upload logs today or tomorrow.
[06:36] Tom Rivera: i'll get it in by Friday.
[06:38] Raj Patel: great. i'll also prepare the SDK sample for function calling with a toy schema that mirrors your downstream ingestion.
[06:46] Alice Nguyen: any dependencies on our infra for the benchmark? for example whitelisted IPs or VPC peering?
[06:51] Jess Carter: for Private/Dedicated pilot we'll want a peering or private endpoint; for hosted we can do IP allowlist. we'll document both.
[06:59] Priya Shah: KMS integration — can you support customer-managed keys in cloud provider X?
[07:04] Raj Patel: yes we support customer-managed KMS across major clouds. if you have an on-prem HSM we can discuss an HSM proxy as well.
[07:12] Marcus Li: curious about rollouts and model pinning. can we pin to a vetted model and do canaries?
[07:18] Raj Patel: yes rollouts are first-class — canary deploys, A/B routes, and automatic fallback to hosted model variants if Dedicated node capacity is limited.
[07:26] Alice Nguyen: cool. last thing — sample code and time to first call, what's realistic for Tom to get a basic chat call working?
[07:33] Raj Patel: if you use our SDK and swap base url, Tom should have a hello-world chat in a few hours. with the sample repo and our quickstart it's usually <1 day to a working integration.
[07:42] Tom Rivera: great.
[07:44] Jess Carter: ok we're hitting the final stretch — let's recap next steps.
[07:48] Raj Patel: i'll upload the SDK examples and function-calling templates by end of week and include a sample structured-output schema file.
[07:54] Jess Carter: i'll send the pilot pricing, SOW and attach SOC2 and security pack, plus scheduling for benchmark runs.
[07:59] Alice Nguyen: we'll upload the logs and prompt sets and confirm folks for the benchmark run.
[08:04] Priya Shah: i'll review the security pack and follow-up with any questions, probably early next week.
[08:08] Marcus Li: thanks all, excited to see the numbers.
[08:10] Jess Carter: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the kickoff.
